::: {.callout-note}
## Scope of this document

This document reviews the **Scenario 5** results: a densified `(n_p, n_t)`
grid (11 participant sample sizes x 9 text sample sizes, log-spaced, vs. the
original 6x5 grid), doubled replicates per cell (100 vs. 50), and a
companion full-grid `b_intercept` sweep (4 target-accuracy values x the same
99-cell grid, Aim-1-only). All three were run overnight
(2026-08-26/27) as background jobs (`run_scenario5_full.R`,
`run_scenario5_intercept_sweep.R`) and are analyzed here for the first time.

**This document does not modify or supersede**
`synthetic-data-power-error-replication-effect-size-sampling-draft-development.qmd`
(the original Aims 1-2 document, covering the 6x5/50-replicate grid and the
first, 4-cell version of the intercept sweep) -- that document is left as-is,
a record of the original analysis, and is cross-referenced throughout below
rather than re-derived. Where this document's numbers differ from the
original's, that is flagged and explained explicitly (see "A grid-density
caveat" below) rather than treated as a contradiction.

All tables and figures below are computed from pre-existing, already-run
results saved in `results_phase2/*_scenario5_*.rds` and
`results_phase2/aim1_scenario5_intercept_sweep.rds` (no full-grid
recomputation happens when this document is rendered); the original 6x5/50
files (`results_phase2/aim{1,2}_{hlva,pcref,interaction}.rds`) are also
loaded, for direct side-by-side comparison at matched sample sizes.
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggdist)
library(scico)
```

## Computational cost and fit accounting

The table below itemizes every model fit behind the Aims 1-2 program to
date -- the original grid, Scenario 5's densified grid, and all three
`b_intercept` sweeps (the original 4-cell version, its ceiling-densification
follow-up, and Scenario 5's full-grid version) -- broken out by phase rather
than left as a single combined total. This table is a cumulative
cost/bookkeeping summary only: every figure and statistic later in this
document is computed from a single phase's fits (almost always Scenario 5's),
not pooled across phases -- the one exception is an explicit side-by-side
comparison at matched sample sizes in the Aim 2 "grid-density caveat"
section, which compares rather than combines the two grids.

```{r}
#| label: fit-accounting-table

fit_accounting <- tribble(
  ~phase, ~n_sweeps, ~n_effect_values, ~n_cells, ~n_reps, ~fits_per_combo, ~notes,
  "Original Aim 1+2 grid (6x5, 50 reps)",       3, 5, 30, 50, 3, "aim1/aim2_{hlva,pcref,interaction}.rds",
  "Scenario 5 Aim 1+2 grid (11x9, 100 reps)",   3, 5, 99, 100, 3, "aim1/aim2_scenario5_{hlva,pcref,interaction}.rds",
  "Original b_intercept sweep (4 cells)",       1, 5, 4, 50, 1, "aim1_intercept_sweep.rds",
  "Ceiling-densification extension (4 cells)",  1, 2, 4, 50, 1, "aim1_intercept_sweep_ceiling_extension.rds",
  "Scenario 5 b_intercept sweep (11x9)",        1, 4, 99, 100, 1, "aim1_scenario5_intercept_sweep.rds"
) |>
  mutate(total_fits = n_sweeps * n_effect_values * n_cells * n_reps * fits_per_combo)

fit_accounting |>
  select(phase, n_sweeps, n_effect_values, n_cells, n_reps, fits_per_combo, total_fits, notes) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Phase", "Sweeps", "Effect values/sweep", "Grid cells", "Reps/cell",
                  "Fits/combination", "Total fits", "Source file(s)"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

cat("\nGrand total fits across the whole Aims 1-2 program to date:",
    format(sum(fit_accounting$total_fits), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

**Estimated vs. observed run time.** Every prior scenario in this program's
cost-estimation planning (`cost-estimate-expanded-grid-replicates-aims1-2-PLAN.qmd`)
assumed the original 4-`furrr`-worker convention, adopted early in this
project when the development machine was found to be under real memory
pressure (swap frequently near-full). Scenario 5 itself was launched with
**8 workers** instead, after a post-restart check immediately beforehand
found 12 CPU cores and 0% swap in use -- headroom that did not exist earlier
in the project and that motivated raising the worker count for this run
specifically, not a general change to the project's convention.

| Run | Estimated (4 workers) | Actual (8 workers) | Estimated core-hours | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scenario 5 main grid (3 sweeps) | ~33h | **~12.2h** (4.1h + 4.05h + 4.03h per sweep) | ~132 | `scenario5_run.log` |
| Scenario 5 intercept sweep | ~2.9h | **~2.01h** | ~11.7 | `scenario5_intercept_sweep_run.log` |
| **Combined** | ~35.9h | **~14.2h** | ~143.7 | |

Doubling the worker count did not simply halve the wall-clock time (a naive
4-workers-to-8-workers halving would predict ~16.5h + ~1.45h = ~18h, not the
observed ~12.2h + ~2.01h = ~14.2h) -- the actual speedup is somewhat *better*
than linear, plausibly because 8 workers on a 12-core machine leaves more
headroom per worker than 4 workers did when memory was tight (less
contention/swapping overhead per fit). No errors were logged in either run;
warnings were the expected `boundary (singular) fit` messages from `n_t`-poor
cells, muffled by the existing `withCallingHandlers()` pattern.

## Loading Scenario 5, the full-grid intercept sweep, and the original grid; shared helpers

```{r}
#| label: load-results

aim1_files_s5 <- c("results_phase2/aim1_scenario5_hlva.rds",
                    "results_phase2/aim1_scenario5_pcref.rds",
                    "results_phase2/aim1_scenario5_interaction.rds")
aim2_files_s5 <- c("results_phase2/aim2_scenario5_hlva.rds",
                    "results_phase2/aim2_scenario5_pcref.rds",
                    "results_phase2/aim2_scenario5_interaction.rds")
intercept_file_s5 <- "results_phase2/aim1_scenario5_intercept_sweep.rds"

aim1_files_orig <- c("results_phase2/aim1_hlva.rds", "results_phase2/aim1_pcref.rds",
                      "results_phase2/aim1_interaction.rds")
aim2_files_orig <- c("results_phase2/aim2_hlva.rds", "results_phase2/aim2_pcref.rds",
                      "results_phase2/aim2_interaction.rds")

all_needed <- c(aim1_files_s5, aim2_files_s5, intercept_file_s5, aim1_files_orig, aim2_files_orig)
missing_files <- all_needed[!file.exists(all_needed)]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop("Missing result file(s): ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

aim1_hlva_s5        <- readRDS(aim1_files_s5[1])
aim1_pcref_s5       <- readRDS(aim1_files_s5[2])
aim1_interaction_s5 <- readRDS(aim1_files_s5[3])
aim2_hlva_s5        <- readRDS(aim2_files_s5[1])
aim2_pcref_s5       <- readRDS(aim2_files_s5[2])
aim2_interaction_s5 <- readRDS(aim2_files_s5[3])
intercept_s5        <- readRDS(intercept_file_s5)

aim1_hlva_orig        <- readRDS(aim1_files_orig[1])
aim1_pcref_orig       <- readRDS(aim1_files_orig[2])
aim1_interaction_orig <- readRDS(aim1_files_orig[3])
aim2_hlva_orig        <- readRDS(aim2_files_orig[1])
aim2_pcref_orig       <- readRDS(aim2_files_orig[2])
aim2_interaction_orig <- readRDS(aim2_files_orig[3])

own_effect  <- c(zHLVA = 0.363, zPCREFp = 0.095, `zHLVA:zPCREFp` = 0.054)
term_levels <- c("zHLVA", "zPCREFp", "zHLVA:zPCREFp")

n_p_grid_s5 <- sort(unique(aim1_hlva_s5$n_p))
n_t_grid_s5 <- sort(unique(aim1_hlva_s5$n_t))
n_p_grid_orig <- sort(unique(aim1_hlva_orig$n_p))
n_t_grid_orig <- sort(unique(aim1_hlva_orig$n_t))

pool_own_effect <- function(aim1_hlva, aim1_pcref, aim1_interaction) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    aim1_hlva        |> dplyr::filter(term == "zHLVA",        effect_value == own_effect["zHLVA"]),
    aim1_pcref       |> dplyr::filter(term == "zPCREFp",       effect_value == own_effect["zPCREFp"]),
    aim1_interaction |> dplyr::filter(term == "zHLVA:zPCREFp", effect_value == own_effect["zHLVA:zPCREFp"])
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = term_levels))
}

aim1_all_s5   <- pool_own_effect(aim1_hlva_s5, aim1_pcref_s5, aim1_interaction_s5)
aim2_all_s5   <- pool_own_effect(aim2_hlva_s5, aim2_pcref_s5, aim2_interaction_s5)
aim1_all_orig <- pool_own_effect(aim1_hlva_orig, aim1_pcref_orig, aim1_interaction_orig)
aim2_all_orig <- pool_own_effect(aim2_hlva_orig, aim2_pcref_orig, aim2_interaction_orig)

aim1_sweep_combined_s5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  aim1_hlva_s5        |> dplyr::filter(term == "zHLVA"),
  aim1_pcref_s5       |> dplyr::filter(term == "zPCREFp"),
  aim1_interaction_s5 |> dplyr::filter(term == "zHLVA:zPCREFp")
) |> dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = term_levels))

# Shared summary helper -- identical to the original document's version.
summarize_p2_metrics <- function(df, group_vars) {
  df |>
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(group_vars))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      power            = mean(excludes_zero, na.rm = TRUE),
      sign_reliability = mean(correct_sign, na.rm = TRUE),
      type_s_rate      = mean(sign_error[excludes_zero], na.rm = TRUE),
      type_m_ratio     = median(inflation_ratio[excludes_zero], na.rm = TRUE),
      median_bias      = median(bias, na.rm = TRUE),
      coverage         = mean(covers_truth, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_fits           = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Shared heatmap helper. Finalized color scheme (superseding the original
# document's labeled-tile, plain-viridis/gradient2 version, after a
# dedicated color-scheme review): tiles only, no in-cell text labels;
# sequential (non-diverging) panels use viridis with `direction` flipped via
# `lower_is_better` so that light/yellow always means "the diagnostic looks
# good" and dark blue/purple always means "the diagnostic looks bad",
# regardless of whether the underlying metric's good end is high (e.g. power,
# sign reliability, coverage) or low (e.g. Type I rate, Type S rate, Type M
# ratio). Diverging panels (median bias) use scico's "vik" palette (dark
# blue <-> white <-> dark red) rather than a plain red/blue gradient2, so
# that "light/center = good, dark extremes = bad" reads consistently with
# the sequential panels even though bias necessarily uses a different hue
# family (no true diverging viridis palette exists). `viridis_option`
# (added in a later review pass) lets one panel use a different member of
# the viridis family -- see panel_type1_s5 below for why Type I rate uses
# this.
plot_power_heatmap <- function(data, fill_var, facet_var = "term", fill_label = "Value",
                                grid_n_p = n_p_grid_s5, grid_n_t = n_t_grid_s5,
                                limits = c(0, 1), label_format = c("percent", "number"),
                                diverging = FALSE, midpoint = 0, squish = FALSE,
                                lower_is_better = FALSE, viridis_option = "D") {
  label_format <- match.arg(label_format)
  oob_fn <- if (squish) scales::squish else scales::censor

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(n_p, levels = grid_n_p), y = factor(n_t, levels = grid_n_t),
                    fill = .data[[fill_var]])) +
    geom_tile() +
    # Square tiles rather than the tall/thin default -- coord_fixed treats
    # each discrete x/y category as one unit, so ratio = 1 forces literally
    # square cells regardless of how many n_p vs. n_t levels there are.
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
    facet_wrap(stats::as.formula(paste0("~", facet_var))) +
    labs(x = "Participant sample size (n_p)", y = "Text sample size (n_t)", fill = fill_label) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6))

  if (diverging) {
    p + scico::scale_fill_scico(palette = "vik", limits = limits, oob = oob_fn)
  } else if (label_format == "percent") {
    p + scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = limits, labels = scales::percent, oob = oob_fn,
                              direction = if (lower_is_better) -1 else 1, option = viridis_option)
  } else {
    p + scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = limits, oob = oob_fn,
                              direction = if (lower_is_better) -1 else 1, option = viridis_option)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: aim1-metrics-vs-x-and-curve-helpers

# Ported from the original document (`...draft-development.qmd`) -- these
# were present there but dropped when this review document was written,
# and are restored here, adapted for Scenario 5's densified grid. The
# effect-size sweep grids themselves are unchanged from the original:
```
